claim: CAS ref-writer exclusivity is established at the mount-lease boundary, after which the ref protocol is single-writer by construction.
The writer's lease-liveness checks use local zero-request `CLOCK_BOOTTIME` fences through `mayMutate` and `refAppendFenceOk`.
Foreign-write detection on the CAS hot path is limited to incidental signals from operations already being performed, such as conditional-PUT token mismatches or unexpected bytes at an owned key.
An incidental interference signal causes `LOGICAL_ERROR`, a fail-closed mount fence, and bounded remount recovery; diagnosis may issue requests only in a background path.
Wall clocks may be trusted to decline lease acquisition, but lease acquisition and fencing establish liveness by observing token stability on the observer's monotonic clock.
A `gc_fenced` lease is a transferable certificate of observed death, so a successor may skip token observation and pay only `materialization_grace_ms`.
`materialization_grace_ms` defaults to 30000 ms and is configurable.
Lowering `materialization_grace_ms` increases the risk that a late-materializing predecessor write is dropped by the recovery seal and later reported as debris.
A self-remount waits for unresolved ref-log conditional PUTs to resolve and owes `materialization_grace_ms` only when at least one ref-log PUT remains unresolved.
The recovery seal is required because `materialization_grace_ms` is an operational store allowance without a documented universal upper bound.
A clean lease release drains all ref-append lanes and writes `released_clean` only after every in-flight conditional PUT resolves within the ordinary request budget.
If clean-release draining leaves an unresolved PUT at the shutdown deadline, the `released_clean` marker is skipped and the successor treats the handover as unclean.
Unclean takeover observes a stable lease token for `mount_lease_ttl_ms * 1.05 + poll_interval_ms` on the observer's monotonic clock before reclaiming with token-guarded `putOverwrite`.
A `released_clean` marker skips observation, `T_mat`, and the recovery seal on ordinary restarts.
An unclean takeover without a GC fence costs approximately `mount_lease_ttl_ms + materialization_grace_ms`, about 60 seconds with the stated defaults, before writable mount opens.
GC fence-out uses token stability on the GC leader's own monotonic clock instead of comparing `MountLease.expires_at_ms` with the leader's wall clock.
A new GC leader starts lease observation afresh, delaying fencing by one round without weakening safety because fencing is a liveness and cleanup mechanism.
The unclean-handover wait must satisfy `unclean handover wait >= all client timeouts + materialization_grace_ms`.
At an unclean mount, recovery LIST and replay are followed by an immediate snapshot PUT seal before the mount opens writable.
The recovery seal ID is `RefTxnId(my_epoch - 1, 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF)`, which covers every late log from every dead epoch below `my_epoch`.
The recovery seal is the only snapshot whose ID is an upper bound of a covered region rather than a real transaction ID.
Recovery seals apply to `Live`-lifecycle tables, while `Removed` recoveries are not sealed and rely on ordinary namespace cleanup for late rebirth debris.
The recovery seal body records `sealed_from`, the greatest transaction ID listed during recovery, so the sweep can identify logs materialized after the recovery LIST.
A failed recovery-seal PUT prevents the mount from opening writable; the next attempt allocates a fresh epoch and a strictly larger seal ID.
`snapshot_min_log_age_ms`, its age gates, `CasRefLatePredecessorObserved`, and young-entry replay bookkeeping are removed from the ref protocol.

Snapshot publication copies the live state once at a transaction boundary when the count threshold exceeds `snapshot_log_count_threshold` or the bytes threshold fires, then encodes and PUTs asynchronously.
The writer retains `fence_ok` verification before and after every conditional ref-log PUT, including `CasConditionalWriteFenceLostPostWrite`.
The orphan sweep can report a `materialization_grace_ms` violation from a log below the seal without reading it to revive the object.
A lane refuses to allocate new IDs past an unresolved PUT in release builds and uses `chassert` for the same wedge invariant in debug builds.
The rev.6 GC-defense audit keeps the `gc/state` CAS, orphan-sweep prior-epoch gate, and fold-lag machinery because they are GC or intra-node mechanisms rather than foreign-writer defenses.
The rev.6 proposal was superseded by the approved rev.6 design because sealing at the greatest listed transaction ID was insufficient.
The rev.5 `snapshot_min_log_age_ms` grace window could leave a late predecessor log visible to cold folds while permanently absent from the writer's state.
The rev.5 five-second grace floor was measured to cause approximately 20–26 GB/hour of ref snapshot traffic per node in the cited soak.
The rev.6 proposal specified a default `materialization_grace_ms` of 30000 ms for unclean handovers and no wait for a drained clean release.
The proposal's recovery-seal-at-listed-maximum rule was later corrected to the dead-epoch upper-bound rule because an unresolved predecessor ID can exceed the greatest listed ID.
The proposal raised `snapshot_log_count_threshold` from 64 to 256 and replaced grace-window replay with copy-once-from-live publication.
The 2026-07-13 soak recorded 1,128,370 PUTs and 5,704,432 GETs across both nodes during the measured window.
Every measured S3 PUT corresponded one-to-one with a controlled conditional write: 1,128,370 PUTs versus 1,133,550 `CasConditionalWriteAttempts` after chaos attempt inflation.
Ref-log appends were about 7% of PUTs and batched 3.5 million logical ref operations at a 43:1 ratio.
Deduplication adoption was 69% in the soak, with about 598,000 adopts versus 264,000 uploads.
Relink fetches consumed about 1,021,705 GETs and 1,957,163 HEADs, with zero blob-body uploads.
`RemovePart` generated zero S3 requests in the soak because removal is a batched ref operation and physical deletion is deferred to GC.
A successful ch1 GC round averaged about 1,850 GETs, 4,720 HEADs, and 1,320 DELETEs.
GC accounted for about 13% of GETs, 20% of HEADs, and nearly all DELETEs, estimated at about 6.5% of the AWS S3 request cost in the run.
The soak measured about 1.96 GB of IO-buffer churn per GC round while useful `ReadBufferFromS3Bytes` reads averaged 24.4 MB per round.
The AWS S3 Standard request-cost estimate was approximately 12.2 dollars for 72 minutes, or about 10 dollars per hour, excluding storage.
The highest-ranked soak optimization lever was reducing per-file relink probes through manifest-hash identity.
Chaos restarts reset `system.events`, so CAS run totals must be computed from summed per-second deltas in `system.metric_log`.
`part_log` aggregates must be filtered by table because system-log-table parts otherwise contaminate workload statistics.
The corrected soak configuration stored every `ca_stress` workload part as Wide on the CA disk, while Compact parts in unfiltered `part_log` belonged to local system-log tables.
A `ca_stress` Wide part wrote about 26.8 files but generated about 5.8 blob-body writes and one manifest write because small files were inlined into the manifest.

The full two-hour chaos soak completed with 38 chaos faults and no product-visible fatal or logical failures; the residual availability classes included 20 `aborted_persistent`, 3 `mount_fenced`, and 1 `s3_transient` outcome.
The scenario stabilization dev campaign completed 35 of 35 scenarios with zero skips, and S13 was the only product regression found and fixed across both campaigns.
The prod-scale scenario campaign was paused by the user after seven scenarios, with five formerly inconclusive priority verdicts resolved at prod scale.
The S01 8 GiB scenario exposed rustfs multipart temporary-space churn with an observed approximate blob ceiling of 2 GiB.
The S03 full-scale scenario exposed rustfs PUT degradation near 6.4 GB of sustained writes and was classified as infrastructure rather than a product failure.
The S31 dry-run tool inspects only shard 0, so its result is a known tool-only gap rather than a CAS product verdict.
S36 is commissioned to test `ALTER TABLE ... MOVE PART|PARTITION TO DISK/VOLUME` in both local-to-CA and CA-to-local directions, including no dangling refs and round-trip deduplication.
S37 is commissioned to test multi-disk policies containing local and CA disks, including mixed-disk merges and atomic restart recovery during policy moves.
A merge upload failure must retry the upload from the staged part rather than rerunning the whole merge.
The unattended campaign classified an `unaccounted`/dangling-precommit orphan discrepancy during chaos recovery as a harness or S30-family follow-up with no data loss observed.
The S38 harness could make `assert_gc_no_failed` vacuous because `observe.py` queried the removed `min_ack` column and swallowed `UNKNOWN_IDENTIFIER`.
A S38 post-restart finding reported `txn_id 2-0 not strictly greater than greatest applied 2-MAX` after a seal `{2,MAX}`, indicating that sequence zero should not exist.
The unattended campaign abandoned the Round-B §5 absence-means-Clean optimization after its spare-clear transition was found unsafe; the shipped round retained §§1–4 and §6.
The `adoptEvidence` relink lifecycle exposure was tracked independently from the abandoned §5 optimization and required a separate investigation.
`adoptEvidence` records a tokenless, bodyless, edgeless dependency during the transaction body, while the destination's durable `precommitAdd` edge is appended only at commit.
A committed-source adopt is not a pending blob, so it is never uploaded by `putBlob`; before `precommitAdd`, the destination contributes no durable in-degree edge to the adopted blob.

The §4 promote gate proves a future GC fold will spare an adopted blob after the destination precommit edge is visible, but it does not prevent a previously captured pre-CAS `deleteExact` from firing.
A resurrect displaces a condemned blob from token `t1` to fresh token `t2`, whereas `adoptEvidence` keeps the original token `t1` and therefore does not make a stale `deleteExact(h,t1)` harmless.
GC redelete runs before the round's `gc/state` CAS and does not re-check recovered in-degree before issuing `deleteExact` for a previously captured `delete_pending` row.
A fresh GC leader's spare is add-only and cannot cancel a stale leader's already-captured pre-CAS delete.
`grabOldParts` removes a CA part only when it is `Outdated` and its `DataPartPtr` is uniquely owned.

Local-source relinks hold the source as a live `DataPartPtr`, so the source replica's edge remains pinned through the destination commit and the exposure is structurally unreachable for those relinks.
CAS refs are per-replica while blobs are pool-wide, so a blob's in-degree counts one edge for each replica manifest that names it.
The fetch-by-relink exposure is limited to a short synchronous `stageManifest` window before `precommitAdd`.
The fetch-by-relink residual requires a `stageManifest` stall across at least two GC folds, every replica dropping the part ref, and a deposed leader firing `deleteExact(h,t1)` after promote.
Commit `8fe6331a431` widened the fetch-by-relink residual by removing promote-time `copyForwardFromCondemned`, which had displaced condemned content to a fresh token.
The recommended root-cause fix for the fetch-by-relink residual is a liveness re-check at the GC pre-CAS `deleteExact` site rather than restoring blanket promote-time HEAD and `loadMeta` probes.
All per-part files are designed to become ordinary manifest tree entries, making the per-ref mutable-file set empty.
`txn_version.txt` is the only genuinely in-place-mutable per-part file identified by the all-tree design.
`uuid.txt` is write-once and checksummed, so changing it in place would break `CHECK TABLE` even on vanilla storage.
`metadata_version.txt` is write-once in current live writers and may legitimately diverge across replicas during `ALTER` metadata-snapshot windows.
Committed-part standalone add and overwrite operations use an audited manifest repoint rather than failing closed or silently doing nothing.
An effective committed-part repoint emits a `system.content_addressed_log` event, a warning-level log, and a ProfileEvent.
On atomic-write storages, `VersionMetadataOnDisk` writes version information with one `writeFile` instead of a temporary file plus rename.
A CA MVCC store event is intended to produce one manifest repoint, and `txn_version.txt.tmp` is never created on CA.
A committed-file unlink stages a removal mark; if the whole part is also removed, the mark is superseded and the normal ref-drop path pays zero repoints.
A standalone committed-file removal without a directory drop publishes one repoint containing the manifest without the removed entry.
The all-tree design closes B123's documented fail-open in which a surgical single-file delete silently did nothing.
A repoint publishes the new manifest closure before backend observation and atomically moves ownership onto the same ref key; the old manifest is reclaimed by normal GC.
A byte-equal repoint is a zero-mutation no-op with no audit event.
The repoint primitive serializes concurrent repoints through the per-table single-writer ref lane and promote CAS.
The all-tree TLA+ safety argument refines a same-key repoint into `WDropRef` followed by `WPromote` on a scratch state, rather than modeling the whole repoint as a dedicated action.
The all-tree T12 unit gate passed 922 tests across 160 suites with zero failures and two pre-existing disabled tests.
The all-tree integration gate passed the RustFS relink test in 23.62 seconds and the CA transaction stateless test with zero failures.
The all-tree soak recorded zero unreachable objects and zero dangling objects at both recovery checkpoints and the final converge checkpoint.
The all-tree relink integration test was migrated from MinIO to RustFS because the `CasProbe` correctly rejects MinIO for not enforcing conditional deletes.
`CasRefRepoint == 0` is a valid soak assertion for cards without `FREEZE`, `ATTACH`, `DETACH`, `MOVE`, or `REPLACE PARTITION`, while attach/detach lifecycle cards legitimately repoint.
The GC defense audit found all six named GC-side sites compliant with the rule that foreign-writer defense spends no speculative S3 requests on hot paths.
The `gc/state` round-ownership re-read is used only for destructive namespace cleanup and checks both per page and per key to prevent mid-page namespace recreation.
Threading the already-held `(state, state_token)` pair to the terminal GC CAS avoids a zombie-steal re-read and costs zero requests.
Per-round LIST hunting for deposed-leader GC debris had already been removed; stale generations are now reclaimed by ordinary retention pruning with zero extra hot-path requests.
The orphan-sweep eligibility gate uses the durable mount watermark to identify dead epochs and treats a missing watermark as not eligible, so it deletes nothing on that fallback.
Orphan-sweep `NotFound` and `TokenMismatch` outcomes are tolerated and logged without retries or re-verification GETs.
Fold-lag clamp barriers do not add request work: they defer cursor advancement and suppress graduation when manifest bodies are not yet visible.
When a listed ref-log body vanishes or fails to decode, GC aborts ref folding for the round and resets cursor advances to already durable parents without issuing diagnostic requests.
The Round-B plan defines `part_folder_validate` as a string setting with `always`, `age <N>`, and `never` modes, defaulting to `always`.

Under `part_folder_validate=age <N>` or `never`, `ForceFresh` may reuse a retained part-folder view after the ref still resolves to the same manifest and mutable-file state without paying the body-existence HEAD.
The Round-B plan defines `dedup_cache_bytes` as an existing cache setting with a documented 64 MiB default and proposes measuring 64 MiB, 256 MiB, and 1 GiB variants.
A dedup-cache hit does not skip the occupancy HEAD; it avoids the body PUT represented by `CasBlobBodyPutAvoided`.

The Round-B plan defines `casSizedReadSettings` to shrink known-size fold read buffers to body size plus 4096 bytes, capped at the caller's base buffer size, while leaving unknown size zero unchanged.
Manifest-trust relink adoption trusts only tokenless dependencies marked `DepEntry.adopted`; a tokenless pending-upload dependency remains fail-closed at promote.
The planned manifest-trust promote path removes per-leaf `head` and `loadMeta` probes for adopted leaves and emits `CasBlobAdoptTrusted` with `reason=manifest-trust`.
The Round-B plan required the absence-means-Clean TLA+ gate to be green before any §5 code and required §5 code to land as one revertible commit.
The abandoned §5 plan proposed making blob meta a pure tombstone where absent meta means Clean, with fresh-body-first resurrect and spare tombstone clearing.
The read-only replica design uses a third CAS mount mode named `reader` that writes only its own `gc/readers/<reader_id>` pin key family and rejects `createTransaction()` with `READONLY`.
A reader serves the folded state `replay(base_snapshot, log tail)` rather than the bare newest snapshot, so read freshness follows log-append latency.
Reader part discovery comes from the adopted snapshot state through readonly refresh and never from a live object-store LIST.
A running read-only replica query holds its `DataPart` objects for the query duration, so concurrent refresh changes apply only to new queries.
Each in-use `DataPart` in reader mode owns an opaque `snapshot_pin` token for its lifetime, and the reader publishes the minimum snapshot over its live tokens as `S_min`.
Reader pin tokens are advanceable: parts still present in a refreshed snapshot advance to the new snapshot, while dropped-but-held parts retain their last valid snapshot.
A durable reader pin at `gc/readers/<reader_id>` contains per-namespace `base_snapshot` and `tail_head` values plus `lease_expiry`.
Reader pins are pool-global, heartbeated, republished at reader start, and ignored by GC after the reader lease expires.
The writer's GC retention floor is the minimum `S_min` over every non-expired reader pin and gates blob reclaim, ref-object cleanup, and namespace cleanup.
Reader retention is implemented as incremental removal deferral rather than refolding the entire pinned closure each GC round.
The writer's snapshot publication policy gains an age trigger so slowly changing tables periodically publish a small snapshot and do not leave readers with an ancient base.
Reader retention is unbounded by a separate `H_max`; active query duration and reader lease TTL are the intended retention bounds.
One long-running query on any reader holds the global pool vacuum floor because the floor is the minimum across all reader pins.
A dropped table or dead pool-member decommission does not reclaim a reader-pinned historical closure until the reader pin releases or expires.
Fetch-by-relink handoff pins and reader snapshot pins share only the GC retention-overlay primitive and are independently shippable features.
The read-only replica's snapshot contract covers immutable part data, manifests, and ref-table state, while `roots/<ns>/_files/*` remains best-effort.
The reader design requires the `IDataPartStorage::snapshot_pin` hook to be nullable and disk-gated so non-CAS and non-reader disks receive `nullptr`.
The reader implementation requires a TLA+ invariant that every object in a live reader pin's `replay(S, tail <= L)` closure is neither condemned nor pruned.
The read-only replica design rejects reader-to-writer promotion, an `H_max` snapshot-age cap, per-blob read pins, and making the reader a full pool member as scope for this design.
The planned §5 spare-heal transition reintroduced the removed `clearSparedMeta` behavior by clearing a tombstone while the blob retained condemn-time token `t1`.
Exact-token deletion protects against different-token resurrection but does not protect against same-token reuse.
A spare that clears a tombstone can advertise a blob as Clean at token `t1`, allowing a stale deposed-leader `deleteExact(h,t1)` to delete the live body.
A token-preserving `adoptEvidence` recovery path can re-reference a condemned blob at token `t1`, invalidating the premise that all in-degree recovery uses fresh-token resurrection.
The original `CaMetaAbsenceClean.tla` gate was false-green because `GcSpareHeal` atomically reset `queuedDeletes`, unlike the real code.
When the model retained queued deletes during `GcSpareHeal`, TLC found 37 states violating `INV_ABSENCE_NO_QUEUED_DELETE`.
The user abandoned §5, no unsafe §5 code landed, and the optimization round shipped §§1–4 plus §6.
Any future §5 revival must keep spare tombstones uncleared until a writer resurrects the blob with a fresh token.
A future §5 revival would require a faithful split-action two-leader TLA+ model and a token-preserving `adoptEvidence` recovery action.
The separate adoptEvidence exposure exists because the destination's durable edge is committed after the body-time adopt evidence and the trusted promote path can defer absent-body detection to fsck.
